div.p: Since general purpose operating systems cannot satisfy all demands of real-time applications, they have been extended. A Windows NT extension for the operation in application of moving picture transmission on a local network is presented. In contrast to commercial extensions, an applicationand scheduling-based extension has been developed. It is targeted to the network and display card. The tool developed for the evaluation of scheduling algorithms has enabled an off-line selection of a combination of scheduling algorithms. RMS and sporadic server algorithms improve functioning of the described multimedia application. The increasing of aperiodic tasks schedulability can cause a decrease of periodic tasks schedulability. By adjusting the sporadic server parameter values we determine minimal server capacity and maximal server period in order to ensure necessary aperiodic tasks schedulability, whereby periodic tasks schedulability should be disturbed as less as possible. The described adjustment procedure enables a faster and safer determination of sporadic server parameters. Carefully selected parameters have enabled further improvement conceming moving picture transmission on a local network.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: Besides functional requests, computer systems must also satisfy real-time requests, which can often be hard. This also holds for personal computers as parts of embedded systems. In such cases timing properties mostly depend on hardware performance and software support. Software support should satisfy demands of a broad spectrum of users. It should also be stable and reliable. It refers specially to an operating system. The problem would be almost solved by a real-time operating system, which is not always possible due to the price, application programs or even tradition. Therefore, real-time extensions to general purpose operating systems have been developed.

The basic motive for the research described in this paper comes from [l], which gives an analysis of extended Windows NT in real-time application. Due to complicated and expensive commercial solutions, an application-based scheduling extension is proposed which reaches measurably better results in a narrower field of application. On the basis of hardware and software measurements, input task sets as well as aperiodic and periodic workloads are determined. The scheduling algorithm is selected off-line by means of a developed simulation too: and a combination of the Rate Monotonic SchedJling (RMS) and the Sporadic Server (SS) algorithm is chosen. The experiment is carried out by using two computers connected on a local network.

The RMS algorithm is dedicated to scheduling of periodic, whereas the SS algorithm schedules aperiodic tasks. The best schedulability of periodic tasks would be reached without aperiodic requests in the mixture of input tasks. By introducing SS the available system capacity is scheduled to aperiodic tasks as well. Aperiodic tasks schedulability is improved directly by increasing the capacity andor decreasing the SS period.

The schedulability increment decreases periodic task set schedulability. By carefklly selecting the SS algorithm parameters we intend to improve aperiodic task schedulability, disturbing thereby periodic task schedulability as less as possible. Two experiments have been carried out in which, besides other constant parameters, capacity, i.e. the SS period, is varied. Then, necessary values of the SS maximal capacity and minimal period are determined. The improvement obtained in this way has also been evaluated at the application level as well as at the operating system level. The experiment was done on Windows NT 4.0 due to a comparison with results obtained in [ 1 3.

The next chapters describe scheduling algorithms and parameters of their evaluation, real-time possibilities with Windows NT, a system of moving picture transmission on a local network, , the procedure of determining the properties of the mixture of tasks and workloads, the procedure of adjusting the S S algorithm parameters, and finally the application evaluation.

div.head: SCHEDULING ALGORITHMS AND EVALUATION
div.p: M S algorithm guarantees satisfaction of hard deadlines of periodic tasks in a real-time system. Regular priorities are assigned to tasks according to the speed of their requests. The algorithm guafantees that n periodic tasks can satisfy its time requests if the utilization of resources used by the tasks is less than n(2"" -1). Other characteristics are in [2].

Algorithms of aperiodic task scheduling must be able to guarantee the deadlines for hard deadline periodic tasks and provide good average response times for soft deadline aperiodic tasks. The following algorithms can be seen in [2]. Two most important approaches to servicing soft deadline aperiodic requests without bandwidth preservation are background processing (BP) and polling server (PS). Algorithms of a deferrabIe server (DS) and a priority exchange server (PE) protect the execution time assigned to aperiodic servicing, i.e. they have bandwidth preservation. A better algorithm must have aperiodic response times measurable by a DS and a PE algorithm; it should be embedded simpler than a DS algorithm and its server size should be greater than the PE algorithm one. That is the sporadic server algorithm (SS). A sporadic server algorithm creates a task of high priority level for aperiodic tasks servicing and protects the execution time at a high priority level until an aperiodic request appears. In contrast to the DS and PE, the SS algorithm sets its server ex'ecution time only after some of the execution time or the whole execution time is consumed. The values of replenished and consumed server execution times are equal. A very significant feature of the SS algorithm is a constant priority level of execution. The SS is equal in behavior as a periodic task and it has reduced risk to enter the critical zone.

Software evaluation tool is described in [3] and shown in the lower part of Figure 2.1. It enables evaluation according to the implemented parameters described below. These parameters enable the best algorithm combination selection through mutual comparison and also adjustment of SS algorithm parameters. Response time (t,) is the time that elapsed from the task execution request to the end of task execution. It can be calculated as the difference between end time and ready time. Resource utilization (0 is equal to the ratio of the task execution time and the task period for any task.
Resource utilization of the mixture of task sets can be calculated as the sum of all ratios of the processor busy time and total simulation time for all iterations.

Server task utilization (UT, ) is the ratio of sums of all server task execution times servicing tasks and the sum of total execution times of server tasks. The number of tasks with missed deadlines (nd) is the number of tasks from the input task sets that missed deadlines, or whose execution time is greater than deadline ( c > t, ). div.head: WINDOWS NT IN RESALTIME APPLICATION
div.p: Windows NT has been designed as a 32-bit, responsive, reliable, general purpose operating system for desktop and business applications. Often it has a real-time extension for the embedded applications. Windows NT is characterized as a soft real-time operating system. According to Figure 2.1, the operating system is situated between application layer and x86 hardware. Applications generate tasks in the application layer. Environment subsystem is a user mode process providing services to applications. It emulates the behavior of a specific operating system and converts requests made by an application to requests understood by NT's kernel. NT Executive contains system services provided by a set of APIs. More details about Windows NT architecture can be found in [4,5]. A better response of real-time applications can also be ' achieved by scheduling higher priority levels to threads of corresponding devices. According to [4,5], there are some fundamental approaches that attempt to adapt the advantages of Windows NT on the demands of realtime. These approaches are used for commercial real-time extensions [5,6], like Intime of RadiSys, HyperKernel of Imagination Systems, RTX of VenturCom, Windows CE and Windows NT Embedded. In contrast to the given commercial solutions, the developed solution is easier and application oriented. Real-time extension is targeted to network and display card and implemented as an extension of their drivers. All processes fiom the application level which request network services and become higher are treated as real-time processes.

The selected algorithm combination (RMS and SS) is placed in one rtschsys Ithat is situated outside the operating system address space, which contributes to the stability of kernel processes. By means of that driver two Dynamic Library Link (dll) files are called as necessary, which handle the network and display cards. Files netx.dl1 and disx.dll use Win32 API standard functions, as well as their own functions enabling a link with standard device drivers. Their own functions also play the role of algorithms, like Rms() and Ss(), and separate periodic and aperiodic demands (Per(), Aper()). The application layer generates a series of demands. For that purpose a real-time extension of Win32 Subsystem is created. It detects the source of a realtime application on the basis of I/O address activation and IORQs generation. These applications are yielded the usage of the mentioned dll files with a higher priority in comparison with others. Priority is precisely given by the implemented algorithms, by which the execution of these applications with nonreal-time applications is enabled. Some ideas come from [4,5,6].

div.head: Experimental Hardware and Data
div.p: All experiments are carried out in the system consisting of two remote computers, which exchange the camera moving picture.

div.head: Acquisition
div.p: In addition to the evaluation tool, Figure 2.1 shows points of incoming parameters acquisition at Windows NT levels. Task parameters are acquired at all levels of the operating system. Depending on the level, this is supported by software and hardware tools. Software tools are counters with different counting resolutions and analysis programs. A logic analyzer supports hardware measurements. Task parameters are indicated through signal appearance but also through thread and process' activities at the application and hardware level. After measurements and counting, the obtained data are processed in order to give numerical values of simulation input parameters. Some of them are execution time, period, interarrival time and corresponding distribution. Also, in the observed interval of system running, workload is determined. These parameters can be seen in [3]. They are set at the level of CPU, memory, handles, threads and processes in the interval of 15 minutes. The workload percentage and number of operations increase with a higher number of the applications run. Some applications are constantly running and are treated as constant or periodic system workload. The other mentioned applications have aperiodic behavior. Active applications are the described acquisition tools, Windows NT, Word for Windows 97 and timing critical applications using network and display resources (Real Player, Net Meeting, FTP). An average value of processor workload is taken, i.e. a high 89%. According to hardware and s o h a r e measurements, 23 periodic and 12 aperiodic tasks are included. The tasks are formed on the basis of the number of threads and processes. The periodic tasks period ranges between 13-99 and the execution time range is 10-71 ps. The aperiodic tasks interarrival time range is 25-78 whereas the execution time range is 5-37 ps. Deadlines of periodic tasks are equal to the period whereas the ones of aperiodic tasks equal the interarrival time. In the previous research sporadic server task had a period of 40 and the capacity of 20p. Current research deals with adjusted SS parameters.

div.head: Sporadic Server Parameters Adjustment
div.p: The SS algorithm is expected to show the best results in the combination with the RMS algorithm.

According to [7], capacity and period determine the behaviour of all fixed priority servers, including SS. Server utilization depends on the selected capacity and better performances are achieved with large capacity. Server period may be larger than the period of the highest priority hard task. div.p: According to [1,5], evaluation at the operating system level is done by dletermining important parameters at the level of processor, process, network, thread, objects and the system in general. This corresponds to the described software activities regarding the acquisition of task properties. Parameter values have on average been better by about 4%. div.head: CONCLUSION
div.p: According to the majority of available sources and own research results, sporadic server belongs to the group of most successful algorithms with fixed priority levels. It is aimed for aperiodic task scheduling. It has been used in the combination with the RMS algorithm for scheduling the mixture of aperiodic and periodic tasks. The selected combination has been embedded in the real-time extension of the Windows NT operating system. The selection of the combination in question resulted from the evaluation done by using our own evaluation tool. Increasing of aperiodic task schedulability can be expected to cause decreasing of periodic task schedulability. In connection with that, adjustment of sporadic server parameter values is an important procedure by which minimal server capacity and maximal server period are determined in order to ensure necessary aperiodic task schedulability with minimum disturbance of periodic task schedulability. The presented adjustment procedure enables further improvement of moving picture transmission on a local network. In contrast to intuitive guessing of parameter values, this procedure enables faster and safer determination of parameter values. It can also be applied to other algorithms generating servep tasks.
